title: How to See a Doctor
summary: Appointments, choosing a clinic and preparing for a consultation.

sections.heading: Choosing care and booking
sections.text: Ask the clinic whether it provides the service you need, whether an appointment is required, what the consultation costs and which insurance it accepts. Confirm the language spoken by the clinician or arrange a trusted interpreter. If you have a registered family medicine centre, ask it about referrals.

sections.heading: Prepare for the consultation
sections.text: Bring identification, insurance documents, relevant medical records and a list of medicines, allergies and questions. Ask your university for its verified medical-office details; no university contact is assumed here.

sections.heading: Understanding a prescription
sections.text: Ask what each medicine is for, how and when to take it, what precautions apply and whom to contact if you have questions. Ask for instructions in a language you understand. A pharmacist can help explain the label.

title: Student Health Insurance Explained
summary: Understand compulsory and private cover, and know what to ask.

sections.heading: Compulsory medical insurance for international students
sections.text: The Kyrgyz Compulsory Medical Insurance Fund (FOMS) says foreign students should obtain a compulsory medical insurance (OMS) policy. Your university can help explain the process and registration with a family medicine centre. Check current eligibility, dates, fees and coverage directly with FOMS before purchasing.

sections.heading: Documents and how to apply
sections.text: FOMS pages currently give conflicting instructions: its policy page lists a passport and a Kyrgyz personal identification number (PIN), while its July 2025 announcement says an identity document is sufficient even without a PIN. Confirm which rule and application method applies to you with FOMS or your university. Keep your identification and payment receipt available.

sections.heading: Coverage and private insurance
sections.text: Ask FOMS which family medicine centre you should register with, what services are covered, what co-payments and exclusions apply, and when your policy begins. If considering private insurance, compare the provider network, emergency cover, exclusions and reimbursement rules. Keep copies of your policy and receipts.

sections.heading: Emergency treatment and help
sections.text: If someone needs urgent help, call 112 or 103 without waiting to check insurance. The FOMS insurance information line is 113. Ask the insurer about claims, documents and payment obligations once the emergency has been addressed.

sources.label: FOMS: application changes for foreign students, 3 July 2025

title: Top Pharmacies and What to Buy
summary: Practical questions to ask when buying medicines.

sections.heading: Prescriptions and buying medicines
sections.text: Ask a pharmacist whether a prescription is required and bring it if you have one. Availability varies; call the pharmacy to check before travelling. Do not assume a particular medicine is in stock.

sections.heading: Generics, brands and equivalents
sections.text: A generic and a brand-name product may contain the same active ingredient. Ask a pharmacist or clinician to check the ingredient, strength, form and suitability before substituting; do not choose an equivalent solely by name or packaging.

sections.heading: Labels and safe storage
sections.text: Ask the pharmacist to explain the instructions, expiry date and storage requirements in a language you understand. Follow the label and keep medicines away from children. Speak to a healthcare professional if you are unsure.

title: Staying Healthy Through Bishkek’s Seasons
summary: Everyday considerations for weather, air quality, food and travel.

sections.heading: Colds and flu
sections.text: Wash your hands regularly and seek advice from a qualified professional if symptoms concern you, become severe or persist. Ask a clinician about vaccination and your individual risk.

sections.heading: Food and drinking water
sections.text: Wash hands before handling food, use safe water and follow local guidance. Keep raw and cooked foods separate and cook food thoroughly. Ask locally about the safety of your drinking water; use a safer alternative if uncertain.

sections.heading: Allergies and air pollution
sections.text: Ask a clinician about persistent allergy symptoms. Air pollution can affect health: check reliable local air-quality information and consider limiting outdoor activity when pollution is high, especially if you are sensitive.

sections.heading: Winter and mountain travel
sections.text: Dress in warm layers and check forecasts. High altitude can cause illness even in healthy travellers. Plan a gradual ascent and learn the symptoms before travel; seek medical help promptly if symptoms are severe or worsen.

title: Mental Wellbeing
summary: Support for homesickness, academic stress and culture shock.

sections.heading: Adjustment and support
sections.text: Homesickness, academic pressure and culture shock can make adjustment difficult. Stay connected with people you trust, make time for rest and ask your university about student support or counselling.

sections.heading: Finding professional help
sections.text: A qualified mental health professional can help you explore support suited to your needs. Ask about language, confidentiality, fees and insurance before booking. If someone is in immediate danger, call 112 or 103.

title: Cultural & Dietary Needs
summary: Discuss food, fasting and religious preferences with your care team.

sections.heading: Food and religious preferences
sections.text: Tell your care team about halal food, allergies, dietary restrictions and religious practices that matter to you. Ask about ingredients and available alternatives when appropriate.

sections.heading: Ramadan and medication
sections.text: If you plan to fast and have a health condition or take medication, discuss your individual circumstances with a clinician before changing meals or medicines. Ask for a plan that takes account of your health and beliefs.
